sections.heading: supplier-compare-agent | Team project · Show Me Your Token | 2026.09
sections.text:
A decision-support agent that turns supplier quotes into comparable evidence. Code produces a reference ranking, the agent makes a recommendation using read-only tools, and a buyer approves or overrides it.

A four-person team project for the NUS-ISS “Show Me Your Agent” hackathon, demonstrated with synthetic supplier data.

Normalizes price, lead time, payment terms, on-time delivery and quality; applies hard constraints before calculating reference scores and negotiation gaps.

Calls a model through an Ollama-compatible gateway and parses JSON tool requests. The agent may depart from the reference ranking when supported by tool evidence; structured output is validated.

Treats quote text as untrusted input, with injection detection, read-only tools, supplier eligibility checks, fallback behavior, and normal and adversarial evaluation cases.

Logs model recommendations, buyer approvals or override reasons, and request IDs. The system recommends; it never places orders.

Project details: /projects/supplier-compare-agent

GitHub: https://github.com/Darrenus/supplier-compare-agent

sections.heading: no-buzzwords | Personal developer tool | 2026
sections.text:
An installable skill and plugin that asks coding assistants to explain mechanisms and use concrete examples. Evaluation checks that clearer wording preserves technical accuracy.

Ten writing rules target vague wording and unnecessary jargon while preserving precise terminology and an appropriate register for expert readers.

Provides a skill, Claude Code plugin configuration and an optional always-on hook for different assistant workflows.

Python scripts manage test cases and a scoring rubric, with reproducible shuffling and anonymization of responses for blind evaluation.

Uses correctness as a separate release gate: a drop greater than 0.1 from the baseline fails the gate even if the total score improves. Cases also test oversimplification and expert contexts.

Provides continuous-integration checks and offline validation of test cases and scoring rules without model calls or credentials.

GitHub: https://github.com/Darrenus/no-buzzwords

sections.heading: coding-agent-from-scratch | Independent open-source project | 2026.10 - Present
sections.text:
A command-line coding assistant built without an agent framework. Repository maps, sandbox escape tests and A/A controls put each design decision to the test.

A native tool-calling ReAct loop with seven tools. SEARCH/REPLACE editing uses a four-tier matching chain to handle whitespace and partial-line drift. Shell commands run inside macOS Seatbelt, with boundaries verified by escape tests. About 1,140 lines of core code under 60 tests, 12 of them on sandbox policy.

The repository map uses tree-sitter definitions and references to build a file graph, then personalized PageRank to rank context for the task. Constraining edges by actual Python imports raised edge precision from 32% to 100% without dropping a true edge. IDF-weighted seeds addressed query understanding.

On a 112-file repository, the map reduced task steps by 21% and input tokens by 33%. Read that next to its noise: an A/A arm put the input-token noise floor at about 26%, so the 33% sits only just above it, and at n=1 the figure was +6%. It describes that controlled experiment, not a guarantee.

The evaluation harness runs an A/A arm by default, putting effects beside their noise floor; this led me to retract an earlier claim. In this architecture, output caps made history compression unnecessary. Sub-agent isolation used 71% more total tokens (184,130 delegated against 107,466 not delegated, a 1.71x ratio) for 22% less main-loop context, with no gain in completion or correctness. Raw traces are committed.

Project details: /projects/coding-agent-from-scratch

GitHub: https://github.com/Darrenus/coding-agent-from-scratch

sections.heading: lumen | Team project · owned the billing and budget subsystem | 2026.09 - 2026.10
sections.text:
An agent that does mathematics research on its own: a lead splits the work among readers, real computation runs in a sandbox, and every step and its cost streams live and can be steered. I owned the layer that makes that spending accountable.

The project (team-built): readers search arXiv, OpenAlex and the OEIS in parallel and run real computation in a network-less Docker sandbox with Python (NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX, Matplotlib). Every step and its cost streams to the browser live, and you can message a running task, stop it, or edit your last message and run it again.

I owned the server-side billing module: a wallet ledger with atomic per-task expenses, an ordered budget responsibility chain, a default per-account cap with an approval flow, Stripe test-mode top-ups with receipts, authenticated encryption for user-supplied API keys, and staff account administration with actor checks.

Why that layer matters: this agent calls models and runs computation on its own, which means it spends money on its own. A budget has to be able to refuse an action before it runs, refusals have to leave a trail, approvals have to be attributable, and ledger ownership has to survive account deletion.

Every feature commit ships with its own test file — ledger, budget chain, Stripe, key encryption, approval lifecycle and HTTP boundaries. Keeping that discipline inside a codebase someone else leads is what I took away from this project.

Attribution: the project is led by ziyangliu-666 (170 commits); I am the second contributor with 32 of about 227. Parallel scheduling, literature search and sandboxed execution were other members’ work.

GitHub: https://github.com/ziyangliu-666/lumen-next

sections.heading: tickwitness | Independent open-source project | 2026.10 - Present
sections.text:
Freeze a scoped quantitative research experiment, audit its replay accounting, and export independently verifiable evidence.

A research claim, its data binding and its execution assumptions are frozen before any replay is allowed, and the resulting evidence bundle can be re-audited offline without installing the replay engine.

The coordinator holds sole research-write authority: original budgets, retries and acknowledgements each leave a trail, and committed outcomes can be reverified without re-execution.

The current trust boundary is M0, a trusted single owner; registered Python source is not executed. M1 restricted isolation is unimplemented, and process supervision and hashes do not constitute a malicious-code sandbox.

The README states two limits plainly: external human reproduction stands at 0 / PENDING, and a bounded search that finds no counterexample is not a proof of robustness.

Project detail: /projects/tickwitness

GitHub: https://github.com/Darrenus/tickwitness

sections.heading: bodycraft-oss | Independent open-source project | 2026.09 - Present
sections.text:
An open-source re-implementation of the five-path retrieval I built at SAIC, with per-path score breakdowns and weights treated as a measurable ranking problem rather than a matter of taste. Design complete, implementation in progress.

Runs filename and path, section title, SQLite FTS5, dense-vector and entity-graph retrieval in parallel. Results merge per file with per-path scores exposed.

Moves hard-coded scoring parameters into hot-reloadable configuration, so weights can be searched against a labelled evaluation set instead of being fixed in code.

Index schemas, configuration and ranking metrics (NDCG, MRR, Hit@K) are covered by 17 tests. The pipeline runs offline without an API key.

The README labels every claim [design] or [built]: no benchmark has run, so this repository reports no measured ranking results. The weight-search method and measured figures from the internal SAIC version belong to that team and are out of scope here.

Project details: /projects/bodycraft-oss

GitHub: https://github.com/Darrenus/bodycraft-oss

sections.heading: Internal spreadsheet Q&A platform | Backend contributor · patent co-inventor — SAIC team platform | 2026.02 - 2026.05
sections.text:
Turns natural-language questions over uploaded spreadsheets into verified SQL, result tables and charts. Structured plans, whitelisted actions and role-based isolation define what the system can execute.

A team platform: FastAPI and SQLAlchemy backend on MySQL, Redis, MinIO and Qwen, with a React front end streaming over SSE. Rolled out to 20+ internal pilot users, whose trial feedback estimated about two hours of manual work saved per person per day.

My scope was the storage and async layer: uploads to MinIO with table metadata in MySQL, a Redis-backed task queue with scheduler and worker processes for ingestion, and Redis caching.

Co-designed and helped build the Planner–Executor refactor. The planner emits only a structured plan — intent, target fields, actions, constraints and failure policy; the executor runs whitelisted actions over a read-only SQL layer with table-, field- and role-level whitelists. The second phase of the refactor was led by other team members.

Co-authored the invention disclosure as one of the inventors, filed June 2026 and under examination; the method gates execution on a pre-execution score in which access compliance is a hard gate. The core was later rebuilt as a native tool inside an open-source agent runtime, exposing only a controlled clarify / result_table / result_chart protocol.

Project details: /projects/spreadsheet-qa

sections.heading: Hybrid UAV Energy Management | Lead algorithm developer | 2023.06 - 2025.06
sections.text:
Designed and implemented the core energy-management algorithms for a hybrid-powered UAV.

Combined rule-based control with model predictive control to allocate power across multiple energy sources during flight.

Built system-level simulation and analysis workflows to examine power output, energy use and control response, then used the results to tune the allocation strategy.

Iterated algorithms and validated control policies to improve power-use efficiency and operating stability in representative mission conditions.

The project was selected for a national undergraduate innovation programme and received dedicated funding, spanning requirements, algorithm design, simulation and milestone evaluation.

Project details: /projects/hybrid-uav

Designed high-fidelity interactive prototypes and organized more than ten user tests. Qualitative feedback and usability observations guided five major design iterations.

Received the course’s People’s Choice award.

sections.heading: KAIST Smart Canteen | Lead prototype designer | 2024.03 - 2024.06
sections.text:
Led the prototype design of a context-aware campus dining system at KAIST.

Defined requirements, system design and implementation around five campus dining scenarios, modelling user context and environmental changes.

Designed and built the Web interface and integrated the IoT platform to ingest, synchronize and visualize live data.

Created a high-fidelity mobile prototype in Figma, showing dining-space layout, crowd density and food options to support dining decisions and operational analysis.
